Commentary.Commentary: We are back for West Indies' reply. Sri Lanka players can be seen to be in a huddle, before they spread out on the field. Followed by Brandon King and Evin Lewis who walk out to open for West Indies. It will be Chamindu Wickramasinghe to start with the new ball.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, West Indies batters have their task cut out. They need to get off to a flier, and make sure to stitch some valuable partnerships in the middle. Sri Lanka on the other hand, will be hoping to pick some early wickets and apply pressure from the get go. Do join us shortly for the second essay to find out how things pan out.

West Indies got off to a strong start with Romario Shepherd striking early inside the Powerplay, followed by Shamar Joseph adding another breakthrough. The spin pair of Roston Chase and Gudakesh Motie bowled tightly in the middle overs to control the run flow. Post the halfway mark, West Indies lost a bit of control over the run flow. Romario Shepherd came back stronger in the death overs and got an important wicket which ensured that Sri Lanka do not cross the 180-run mark. He stood out with the ball with his two wickets.

Sri Lanka posted a competitive total after a cautious start. Despite losing early wickets, they recovered through key partnerships in the middle overs. Charith Asalanka led from the front with a captain’s knock. Sri Lanka found themselves in early trouble after being put in to bat, with Nissanka and Kusal Perera falling quickly. However, the duo of Mendis and Kamindu steadied the ship with a 31-run stand, followed by an 82-run partnership between Kamindu and Asalanka. Although Kamindu Mendis was dismissed after his half-century, Asalanka continued to anchor the innings, finding a reliable partner in Bhanuka Rajapaksa to push the total into competitive territory. They could've even gotten to 190 if these two were on the crease till the final delivery.

Maheesh Theekshana finishes things off in style for Sri Lanka. A boundary off the very last delivery, and the hosts head into the break with the momentum on their side. West Indies started positively with the new ball, but might feel that they lost their way in the middle overs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Consecutive boundaries, and on both occasions the batters wasn't in control. Romario Shepherd follows the batter with a full one, outside leg. Pathum Nissanka goes back, and gets it to fine leg off the inside edge. The ball runs down to the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Romario Shepherd to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! EDGY! First boundary for Sri Lanka. It is a bumper, angled into the body once again. Pathum Nissanka backs away a bit, and swings hard across the line. The ball catches the top-edge and flies over the keeper's head for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Romario Shepherd to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Romario Shepherd starts with a short ball, around middle. Kusal Mendis pulls it to deep square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Romario Shepherd to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short ball, outside off. Kusal Mendis cuts it to deep point for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Shamar Joseph to Kusal Mendis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: LEG BYE! It is a length ball, nipping in from outside off. Pathum Nissanka is cramped for room. He looks to defend it out from inside the crease but misses. The ball goes in front of slip off the thigh pads. They cross for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Shamar Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off. Pathum Nissanka punches it to point off his back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Shamar Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Shamar Joseph errs in his line this time. He goes very full, but way down the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Shamar Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off. Pathum Nissanka lets it be.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Shamar Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A length ball, around off, shaping away a bit. Pathum Nissanka gets it through cover-point off outer half. They take two runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Shamar Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Shamar Joseph starts his spell with a peach of a delivery. It is good-length ball, that lands outside off and nips away just a bit. It is a scrambled seam delivery. Pathum Nissanka gets on his toes and looks to block it away but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Shamar Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will share the new ball? Shamar Joseph to attack from the other end.
CLOSE! It is a short ball, outside off. Mendis frees his arms and goes for the cut shot, but gets beaten on the outside edge this time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Alzarri Joseph to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: LEG BYE! Good length, angled into the pads. Pathum Nissanka is caught inside the crease, as this skids through. He looks to flick it away but misses. The ball rolls towards short fine off the thigh pads. They collect a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Alzarri Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: This is full, wide of off. Kusal Mendis bunts it to the right of extra covers. Rovman Powell makes a meal of it as he dives over it. The batters take three runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Alzarri Joseph to Kusal Mendis, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Good length this time, outside off. This one nips away a bit. Kusal Mendis looks to hit it away from his body but gets beaten on the inside edge here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Alzarri Joseph to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! It is a bumper this time, sliding down leg. Kusal Mendis looks to hook it away but misses. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Alzarri Joseph to Kusal Mendis, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Alzarri Joseph dishes a full ball, inswinging as well. Kusal Mendis stays deep inside the crease and blocks it into point. Right under his eyes as well.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Alzarri Joseph to Kusal Mendis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pathum Nissanka and Sri Lanka open their account instantly. It is a length ball, outside off. Nissanka waits for it, opens the face late and guides it down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Alzarri Joseph to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we are done with all the pre-match proceedings. This 3-match T20I series is set to kick-off. West Indies players stride out and take the field. Followed by Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis who stride out to open for the hosts. It will be Alzarri Joseph to start with the new ball.

The crowd has turned up in huge numbers. The cheers only get louder as the two teams stride out and line-up for their respective national anthems. It is going to be West Indies' first, followed by one for the hosts.

Charith Asalanka, the captain of Sri Lanka says that they would have opted to bowl first as well, considering the weather conditions. He expressed his anticipation for beginning the preparations for the 2026 World Cup.

Rovman Powell mentioned that West Indies will bowl first due to the uncertain weather conditions and the wet field. He expressed hope that the bowlers could take advantage of the conditions. Reflecting on the team's recent form, Powell added that they have performed very well over the last 12 to 15 months.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Evin Lewis, Brandon King, Shai Hope (WK), Roston Chase, Romario Shepherd, Rovman Powell (C), Sherfane Rutherford, Shamar Springer (On T20I Debut), Alzarri Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Shamar Joseph.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Kusal Mendis (WK), Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Perera, Kamindu Mendis, Charith Asalanka (C), Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Wanindu Hasaranga, Chamindu Wickramasinghe, Maheesh Theekshana, Matheesha Pathirana, Asitha Fernando.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of West Indies. They will BOWL first.

UPDATE 1.15 pm GMT - Well, well! We get a warm welcome here in Sri Lanka. The toss has been officially delayed due to wet outfield. It has now been rescheduled to happen at 1.30 pm GMT, with the play to begin at 2 pm GMT. So stay tuned for the toss.

How is the weather you ask? The weather is clear at the moment with some cloud cover, but there has been rain earlier today and over the past few days. One of Sri Lanka's practice sessions was even washed out. The covers were on, but they’re being removed now, and we’re hopeful for an on-time start.

In contrast, the West Indies have come into this series missing several key players, including stars like Nicholas Pooran and Shimron Hetmyer, who opted out for personal reasons. While this weakens the team's lineup, it also provides an opportunity for other players to step up and make their mark. Despite lacking some of their big names, the West Indies still have quality in their ranks, but the team’s relative inexperience could make their task harder against a more balanced and experienced Sri Lankan squad. To find out how things pan out, do stick around as the toss is just around the corner.

The West Indies cricket team has arrived in Sri Lanka for a limited-overs series, which includes three T20 internationals followed by a three-match ODI series. The series kicks off in Dambulla, a venue known for its slow and dry pitches, which usually favor spin bowling. Playing in home conditions, the Sri Lankan side goes into the series as firm favorites, particularly as most of their star players are available and in form. With familiarity of the conditions on their side, Sri Lanka is expected to be a dominant force throughout the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

After a dominant clean sweep in Tests against New Zealand, Sri Lanka are all set to host West Indies in what promises to be an action-packed three-match T20I series, followed by a three-match ODI series. The spotlight now shifts to the shorter format, with the first T20I set to unfold at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium in Dambulla. Both teams come in with fresh faces, adding new layers of excitement to the contest. Sri Lanka have made some interesting changes, including the return of Bhanuka Rajapaksa, the power-hitter who strengthens the middle order. Chamindu Wickramasinghe keeps his spot in the squad, while Dilshan Madushanka and Dushmantha Chameera miss out. Fresh off a great Test series, Dinesh Chandimal retains his place and could potentially feature in the playing XI. Sri Lanka’s spin attack remains their biggest weapon, with Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana ready to weave their magic. West Indies, on the other hand, have undergone significant changes. Key players like Nicholas Pooran, Andre Russell, and Shimron Hetmyer are unavailable, leaving a revamped squad under the leadership of Rovman Powell. However, the return of Evin Lewis and a fully fit Brandon King provides much-needed experience at the top. This series also offers golden opportunities for newcomers, Terrance Hinds and Shamar Springer to shine and make their marks on the international stage. In the bowling department, Gudakesh Motie shoulders the spin duties, while Alzarri Joseph makes his way back and adds pace to the attack. With all three T20I matches set to take place at the same venue, both teams will be keen to start strong and take an early advantage. While Sri Lanka will be tough to beat on home soil, West Indies have the talent to challenge them if they seize the opportunities. Who are you backing for the win? We’re about to find out soon!
